text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The peak tourist season has begun - some 120,000 tourists crossed the Croatian border last weekend and some 41,000 cars travelled on the road linking Zagreb with the coast.

- Croatian Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa meets his Spanish counterpart Jose Maria Aznar in Madrid where they are expected to sign three bilateral agreements -- on stimulating investment and its protection, on air traffic and on cooperation in the areas of culture, science and education.

- Croatia will use all legal means to fight against the subpoena issued by the U.N. war crimes tribunal, says Croatian ambassador to the Netherlands Jaksa Muljacic. The subpoena called on Croatia to hand over state documents providing information on Bosnian Croat General Tihomir Blaskic.

- Some 15 people contract AIDS every year in Croatia. Despite a Health Ministry recommendation, many medical institutions refuse to offer full medical treatment to the diseased, says head of the AIDS centre Miroslav Lisic.

- Croatia may pay a lot for the ticket to enter the World Trade Organisation (WTO), but now there is no return. Last week it held bilateral talks with the U.S. which demanded the protection of intellectual property and tariff concessions on goods and services.
- Current talks on the succession of former Yugoslav assets may be stopped, says head of the Croatian team Bozo Marendic.

- Although Croatia's insurers recorded a 10 percent increase in premiums in 1996 and their pre-tax profit rose 20 percent, three insurers -- Mediteran, Adria and Royal posted a loss totalling 12.4 million kuna.
- A hundred drivers' licences were taken away by police because of alcohol.

- It is important for everyone to return -- UN ambassador to Croatia Peter Galbraith and to the United Nations Bill Richardson visit Eastern Slavonia. The next two months will be decisive for reintegration, Bill Richardson underlined.

- Radio 101 has to sign a new agreement with the telecommunications council to get a broadcasting licence, but it has first to register with the Court of Commerce. The main problem is the radio's base capital which the court wants to see increased.
- Inspectors are sharpening controls over black-economy workers on building sites.

- Croatia has already made an ambitious plan to promote Croatian tourism in 1998 which foresees one million more tourists, mostly Germans and Italians. Tourist trade suffered a loss of 17.5 billion kuna during the war, says head of Croatian Tourist Association Marijan Bulat.

- The Croatian securities commission has set down 10 rules to regulate the securities market and protect investors. - "Odds are 65-35 for us," says Croatia coach Marijan Vlak ahead of his club's first post-war match with Belgrade's Partizan. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
